title: Blind signatures from one-way functions alone
formal: Does the existence of arbitrary one-way functions imply a classical plain-model blind-signature scheme with concurrent blindness and one-more unforgeability, allowing polynomially many interaction rounds and non-black-box constructions?
definitions:
The security parameter is lambda, supplied in unary. Efficient algorithms are uniform probabilistic polynomial-time Turing machines; security is against nonuniform probabilistic polynomial-size circuit families with polynomially many oracle queries. A function is negligible if it is eventually smaller than lambda^{-c} for every constant c>0. All message, instance and witness lengths in a security experiment are polynomial in lambda. No random oracle, trusted hardware or additional computational assumption is available.

One-way functions means that a uniformly polynomial-time computable family f_lambda:{0,1}^lambda to {0,1}^{ell(lambda)}, for some polynomially bounded output length ell, exists such that every adversary given f_lambda(U_lambda) finds any x-prime with f_lambda(x-prime)=f_lambda(U_lambda) with only negligible probability. Inverters know lambda and must output a lambda-bit preimage. The function need not be injective or a permutation.

KeyGen generates a signer key pair (pk,sk). A polynomial-round interactive protocol between Signer(sk) and User(pk,m) gives the user a signature sigma or an abort symbol. Deterministic Verify(pk,m,sigma) checks signatures. Messages have polynomial length. Honest executions yield accepted signatures except with negligible probability. The scheme has no CRS or globally accessible oracle.

Blindness is tested against a malicious signer that chooses a public key and two equal-length messages m0,m1. A hidden uniform bit b assigns mb to one honest-user session and m(1-b) to another. The signer interleaves both sessions arbitrarily with any further polynomially many sessions on messages of its own choice. If both challenge users finish, it receives their final signatures ordered by message (m0 first, m1 second), without session labels; if either aborts it receives only the common failure notification instead of either signature. Together with its entire interaction view, this must give only negligible advantage in guessing b. Honest users verify signatures before reporting success; malformed public keys may lead to abort.

For one-more unforgeability a malicious user interacts with an honest signer under an honest public key in any polynomial number q of sessions, scheduled concurrently. It wins by outputting q+1 accepted message-signature pairs with pairwise distinct messages. Here q counts all sessions initiated, including aborted sessions; no stronger completed-session accounting is required. The win probability must be negligible for every polynomial-size adversary. Signer sessions use fresh random coins. This fixes the session-count convention explicitly. Signatures need not be unique, and no ideal-world universally composable security or extraction is demanded.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked construction and correctness, blindness and one-more-unforgeability reductions from arbitrary one-way functions, or refute the unrestricted implication. Black-box-only separations and constructions in a global random-oracle model do not settle the plain-model target.
context: Katz, Schröder and Yerukhimovich rule out black-box constructions from one-way permutations, even under weak requirements. Their theorem is a restricted construction barrier, not an unrestricted impossibility result.
why: This asks how little computational hardness suffices for anonymous authenticated transactions.

import_provenance.original_title: Blind signatures from one-way functions alone
import_provenance.original_statement: Does the existence of one-way functions imply classical blind signatures in the plain model, with blindness and one-more unforgeability against polynomial-time adversaries? Allow arbitrary polynomially many rounds and non-black-box techniques, but no trusted setup or ideal random oracle.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Editorial continuation of Chaum’s blind-signature primitive. The 2011 impossibility concerns black-box constructions; the 2026 OWF-based construction uses a global non-programmable random oracle and therefore does not settle the plain-model question.

sentences: A signer issues signatures without learning which messages are being signed.
Blindness must survive interleaved sessions and malicious signer behavior.
A user initiating q signing sessions must not obtain signatures on q+1 distinct messages.
The selected game counts initiated sessions, including aborts.
The target permits non-black-box methods but assumes no global random oracle or trusted setup.
